bottom_line: The Fed, the people who set interest rates, is getting ready to raise rates again because prices keep climbing faster than it wants. That means loans, credit cards and mortgages are likely to get more expensive, on the same day the stock market got shaken by Anthropic's record debut and a 1,000-point Dow drop.

stories.title: The Fed plans more rate hikes
stories.real: Notes from the Fed's last meeting show almost all officials expect more rate hikes, and a bigger hike is still on the table. Fed officials say inflation, meaning how fast prices rise, is 'way higher' than their 2% target, and the AI data-center building boom is pushing prices up too. J.P. Morgan expects hikes at the next three meetings.
stories.you: Borrowing money for a car, house or credit card balance is likely to get more expensive, not cheaper.

stories.title: Anthropic's record stock debut
stories.real: Anthropic, the company behind the Claude AI chatbot, started selling shares on the Nasdaq. Its stock jumped 27% on day one and its total value passed $2 trillion. The same day, the Dow fell 1,000 points as investors cashed out of other stocks, and the S&P 500 was heading for a sixth straight losing day.

stories.title: Nvidia's boss steps away
stories.real: Jensen Huang stepped away from Nvidia, the giant AI chip company, and its stock crashed. Nvidia is tied to so many other companies that people worry the damage could spread. Rival chipmaker AMD also fell after a short-seller, someone who profits when a stock drops, accused it of links to a blacklisted Chinese company. AMD says it follows U.S. law.
stories.you: Many retirement and index funds hold big chunks of chip stocks, so trouble here can hit regular savers.

stories.title: Australia is losing jobs
stories.real: Australia's unemployment rate jumped to 4.9%, a four-year high, after its central bank raised rates. Some experts now say the country has one foot in a recession, meaning the economy is shrinking.
stories.you: It's a real-world example of what can happen to jobs when rates go up to fight inflation.

stories.title: Walmart wins despite fuel costs
stories.real: Walmart raised its sales forecast, helped by pickup and delivery orders, even as fuel costs soar. Its CEO says the plan is to keep prices low anyway.
stories.you: Higher fuel costs are squeezing shoppers and stores, and big retailers are fighting to keep everyday prices down.
